lines.line: An inch of time is an inch of gold. You're spending some now.
Yet we keep saying 'tomorrow.' Thai calls it: put off the day, promise tomorrow.
lines.credit: ผัดวันประกันพรุ่ง · Thai idiom

lines.line: Yesterday is gone. Tomorrow hasn't come. Today is the day to work hard.
lines.credit: The Buddha · Majjhima Nikaya 131, tr. Sujato

lines.line: Still dancing at 100, she heard 'I wish I could.' Her answer: do it.
But our minds wander almost half the time, which is linked to less happiness.
The fix: give each thing your whole mind. On the mat, only the mat.
Health comes first. It is the root of goodness, wealth, joy and inner freedom.
Exercise like brisk walking, up to 75 minutes weekly, went with 1.8 more years.
lines.credit: S. C. Moore et al. · PLoS Medicine, 2012

lines.line: Long life brings joy: each day you learn, each month you can do more.
Now is the only time you can use. So spend it on the mat.
You don't know what today will bring. Nobody does. So now what?
Heat and cold, joy and pain: they come and go. Meet them bravely.
Bernstein, 25, studied the music just in case. Next day, he led the orchestra.
Was he lucky? Chance only helps the mind that is already prepared.
Prepared how? Japanese sport has one word for three things: mind, skill, body.
Body first: eight weeks of yoga went with more strength and flexibility.
Then the mind: ups and downs touch it, but it does not tremble.
lines.credit: The Buddha · Sutta Nipata 2.4, tr. Sujato

lines.line: Speck by speck: pile up dust, and you get a mountain.
Guruji said: practise without fail, and body, mind and spirit grow happy.
lines.credit: K. Pattabhi Jois · Yoga Mala, Preface 1997

lines.line: Your morning mat is your 'just in case.' Ashtanga works quietly, slowly but surely.
Even the sun is new every day. Today has never happened before.
Good news: bouncing back is not rare. It is made of ordinary, everyday strengths.
So build them early: ready your sledge in summer, your cart in winter.
Ants know it too: small, not strong, yet they store food in summer.
At 15, Amundsen trained in the snow every free day, years before his adventures.
lines.credit: Roald Amundsen · My Life as an Explorer

lines.line: Strong, but not stiff: the willow bends under snow and does not break.
Then the mind: whatever comes, keep doing your work, steady and brave.
The Buddha's last words: everything changes, so keep practising with care.
lines.credit: The Buddha · Digha Nikaya 16, tr. Sujato

lines.line: Missed a day? In one study, one miss did not spoil the habit.
lines.credit: Lally et al. · Eur J Soc Psychol, 2010

lines.line: Morning Ashtanga is your summer sledge. Practise for years: peace is coming. No problem.
lines.credit: Pattabhi Jois · recalled by Kino MacGregor

lines.line: At 14, strings snapped on two violins mid-concert. Midori never missed a note.
Strings snap. Joy and sorrow both come. Accept them with a calm, content mind.
The lesson? Prepare ahead, and there is nothing to worry about.
lines.credit: 有備無患 · Chinese, Japanese, Korean idiom

lines.line: An old Thai saying: buy a buffalo at ploughing time, and you pay more.
Start with the body: asana should be firm, and pleasant too.
Then the mind. Hancock hit a wrong chord. Miles breathed and made it right.
We suffer more often in our minds than in real life.
lines.credit: Seneca · Letters to Lucilius 13, tr. Gummere

lines.line: Almost daily, same place: in one study, habits like this went with less stress.
lines.credit: Wood et al. · J Pers Soc Psychol, 2002

lines.line: Yoga is 99 percent practice, 1 percent theory, Guruji said. So live it daily.
lines.credit: R. Sharath Jois · Yoga Mala foreword, 2009

lines.line: Sting: after morning yoga, more energy, more done, a calmer mind. Your turn tomorrow.
Every day is a good day. Even a day that surprises you.
Maybe you'll eat, maybe you'll fast. Guruji said: each morning, wake up and practise.
lines.credit: Pattabhi Jois · recalled by David Williams

lines.line: So train on the calm days, and you stay steady when hard ones come.
lines.credit: Seneca · Letters to Lucilius 18, tr. Gummere

lines.line: Why? Pain that has not come yet is pain you can still avoid.
Wally Funk said her body and mind were ready. At 82, she reached space.
Astronauts practise things going wrong, again and again. So when it happens, no panic.
Japan has a word for it: heijoshin, the everyday mind that stays steady.
Keep planting seeds, morning and evening. You never know which one will grow.
A day's plan lies in its morning. A life's plan lies in steady effort.
One Ashtanga student said: practice makes me better at facing life's challenges.
Young or old, we expect little change ahead. Researchers call this an illusion.
Every body has hard days. The wise expect them, and stay calm.
lines.credit: Tiruvalluvar · Tirukkural 627, tr. G. U. Pope

lines.line: A climber called Grandma Whitney took up jogging. Why? It made climbing much easier.
So pack before you go. Out for a day? Take bread for a week.
First in the bag, a strong body. The mind cannot carry the load alone.
lines.credit: Montaigne · Of the Education of Children

lines.line: Next, a breath habit: slow, deep and steady, until the mind finds balance.
And a mind like a mirror: it meets everything and holds on to nothing.
lines.credit: Zhuangzi · ch. 7, tr. H. A. Giles, 1889

lines.line: But stored bread is not eaten bread. Only what you practise becomes you.
So practise every day. Busy? Do one asana. But never skip completely.
Your daily bread: Ashtanga. Asana for strength, breath for lightness, turning inward for calm.
lines.credit: Gheranda Samhita 1.10-11 · tr. S. C. Vasu

lines.line: Every day brings hidden gifts. Leave them unused, and it quietly takes them back.
lines.credit: Ralph Waldo Emerson · Works and Days, 1870

lines.line: We want to know what's inside. But it's all uncertain. So, be patient.
lines.credit: Ajahn Chah · Not Sure!, Dhamma talk

lines.line: Patient, not idle: young Iyengar began yoga to grow strong for life's challenges.
lines.credit: B. K. S. Iyengar · Light on Life, 2005

lines.line: The body needs a little work each day, never too tiring, never forced.
lines.credit: Quoted by Sun Simiao · Qianjin Yaofang, c. 652

lines.line: And after 40, a more flexible body went with more flexible blood vessels.
lines.credit: Yamamoto et al. · Am J Physiol, 2009

lines.line: Not proud in success, not crushed in defeat. Whatever comes, never lose heart.
Daily 13-minute meditation eased bad moods and sharpened focus, but only after 8 weeks.
lines.credit: Basso et al., NYU · Behav Brain Res, 2019

lines.line: Musicians say: skip practice one day, you notice. Skip three, everyone notices.
And years of steady yoga, it is said, build an unshakable mind.
lines.credit: William James · The Energies of Men, 1907

lines.line: Shaping each day is the highest art. Open tomorrow's gifts on your Ashtanga mat.
